input.task:
Definition lists do not insert required newlines
If the HTML input does not contain any newlines around definition list tags:

```python
import markdownify

md = markdownify.MarkdownConverter().convert

print(md("""
text<dl><dt>Term 1</dt><dd>Definition 1</dd><dt>Term 2</dt><dd>Definition 2</dd></dl>text
""".strip()))
```

then the Markdown output is also missing newlines:

```markdown
text
Term 1
:   Definition 1
Term 2
:   Definition 2
text
```

New lines are required before/after `<dl>` tags and before `<dt>` tags as described here:

https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#definition-lists

https://michelf.ca/projects/php-markdown/extra/#def-list

input.task:
Allow Spark DataFrame Parameters
In Spark, it's allowed to use brackets to reference DataFrames, which cannot be parsed by SqlGlot:

```python
import sqlglot

print(sqlglot.parse_one("""select * from test where id={id} """, dialect="databricks").sql("databricks")) # works fine
print(sqlglot.parse_one("""select * from {df} """, dialect="databricks").sql("databricks")) # fails
```

See also: https://www.databricks.com/blog/parameterized-queries-pyspark

input.task:
Support Oracle/Postgres `XMLNAMESPACES` syntax
Is your feature request related to a problem?
Currently SQLGlot does not support adding namespaces using `XMLNAMESPACES` within the function `XMLTABLE`. This feature is very useful, especially with complex XML's. It makes the overall SQL query much easier to read.

An example of query would be (Postgres example):
```
WITH xmldata(data) AS (VALUES ('
<example xmlns="http://example.com/myns" xmlns:B="http://example.com/b">
 <item foo="1" B:bar="2"/>
 <item foo="3" B:bar="4"/>
 <item foo="4" B:bar="5"/>
</example>'::xml)
)
SELECT xmltable.*
  FROM XMLTABLE(XMLNAMESPACES('http://example.com/myns' AS x,
                              'http://example.com/b' AS "B"),
             '/x:example/x:item'
                PASSING (SELECT data FROM xmldata)
                COLUMNS foo int PATH '@foo',
                  bar int PATH '@B:bar');
```
I will attach a PR.

I have tested the queries against a working Oracle and Postgres DB.

Official Documentation
[Postgres docs: XMLTABLE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-xml.html#FUNCTIONS-XML-PROCESSING-XMLTABLE)
[Oracle docs: XMLTABLE](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/sqlrf/XMLTABLE.html)

input.task:
Non obvious circuit breaker "name" property behavior
If you don't pass a "name" argument you can end up with a TypeError:

```python
cb = CircuitBreaker()
str(cb)  #TypeError: __str__ returned non-string (type NoneType)
```

Of course you have no problem if you first decorate something:

```python
cb = CircuitBreaker()

@cb
def some_func(): ...

str(cb)  # no error
```

But is it really obvious that it ends up with the name of a function?

```
print(cb.name)  # some_func
```

And if you use the same circuit breaker to decorate something else, it's name won't change:

```python
@cb
def another_func(): ...

print(cb)  # still "some_func"
```

I suggest that if there is no name we should generate one on instance initialization instead:

```python
cb = CircuitBreaker()
str(cb)  # unnamed_CircuitBreaker_1
```

Duplicate negative shown in help for a “bool | None” parameter
The following minimal example:

```
import cyclopts
from typing import Annotated

app = cyclopts.App()

@app.default
def cmd(
    *,
    param: Annotated[bool | None, cyclopts.Parameter(negative=“—negative”)] = None,
):
    pass
```

Shows a duplicate `—negative` in the help text when you simply pass `—help` to the command.

From what I can tell, it’s an issue with the union with None, as the same example with a simple bool type does not exhibit this issue.

input.task:
Lazy command loader changes a subapp's `--help` output
Without lazy loading:
```py
# a.py
import cyclopts

app = cyclopts.App("App")
subapp = cyclopts.App("greet")

@subapp.default
def greet(name: str):
    """Greet a person by name."""
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")

app.command(subapp)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()
```
```console
❯ uv run a.py greet --help
Usage: App greet NAME

Greet a person by name.

╭─ Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *  NAME --name  [required]                                              │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```
With lazy loading:
```py
# a.py
import cyclopts

app = cyclopts.App("App")
subapp = cyclopts.App("greet")

@subapp.default
def greet(name: str):
    """Greet a person by name."""
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")

app.command("a:subapp", name="greet")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()
```
```console
❯ uv run a.py greet --help
Usage: App greet NAME

Greet a person by name.

╭─ Commands ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --help -h  Display this message and exit.                               │
│ --version  Display application version.                                 │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *  NAME --name  [required]                                              │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```
Notice how the `--help` output changed, it now includes `--help` and `--version`. These flags were removed from a subapp's `--help` output in [v3.10](https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/releases/tag/v3.10.0) (https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/363) so this seems to be a regression that only appears when a subapp is lazy loaded.
